analyst_view.overall: Kairat (27th of 36, two points) host Mjällby (9th, seven points and unbeaten in the competition) in Almaty and need a win to get out of the elimination places, under interim coach Zhora Arutyunyan, who says he plans changes to the lineup and shape to improve the attack after a 1-1 at Atalanta. Kairat's domestic season is over, so they have had about three weeks without a competitive game; their weak recent shooting and leaky defence (14 conceded in six, including 1-5 at home to Panathinaikos) are already in the numbers, and only Jorginho is out. Mjällby made the longest trip in the club's history (about 16 hours via Istanbul, arriving Monday) and still have a league finale at Halmstad on Sunday, though their league place is settled. New since the last view: Bollsvenskan reports forward Jacob Bergström, one of their two top scorers, is out with a hamstring strain from the Malmö game and misses this match; the numbers only know about Dalsgaard and Stavitski. Polish referee Paweł Raczkowski's low card record (3.8 a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already trim Kairat for scoring only 3 in their last six. Bergström, Mjällby's joint top scorer, is now confirmed out with a hamstring strain, which the numbers don't know about, so I take a little off Mjällby's side, to about 2.1 overall. Kairat's three-week break and promised attacking changes pull both ways, so the size stays small.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners, already cutting Kairat for winning only 12 in their last six and lifting Mjällby a little for 17 in their last three. Kairat should push at home as they need the win, while Mjällby, the in-season side, can keep the ball; the near-even split (4.4 to 4.3) already reflects that, and Bergström's absence matters little for corners, so I stay at 8.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards, already taking a little off for referee Paweł Raczkowski (3.8 cards a game in six on record) and for Mjällby's tidy recent record. There is no rivalry between the clubs, the two have never met, and a Kairat side that must win could foul more if they fall behind, but that is only a hunch, so I stay at 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots and already take about 7% off Kairat for their low recent shooting. I trim a little more, to about 24.1, because Kairat have had no competitive game for around three weeks under an interim coach, and Mjällby are without Bergström after a 16-hour trip with a league game on Sunday; the numbers can't see either.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, already cutting Kairat by about 10% for only 14 on target in six and lifting Mjällby for their accurate recent shooting. With Bergström, one of Mjällby's two top scorers, confirmed out and Kairat short of match rhythm, I go a bit lower, to about 8.0.
